claim: In a heterotic Z3 orbifold the centre of the fixed-point flavour Heisenberg group 3^(1+2d) is the point-group selection rule, so a state of the theta^k twisted sector carries central character omega^k. The central-character doublet V1 + V2 of the W(3,3) Pauli group is therefore the pair of twisted sectors T1 + T2, and the outer inversion's block swap is their exchange. Two physical operators realise the inversion: the unitary S3 reflection (X -> X^-1, Z -> Z), an element of the space group that projects the spectrum, and antiunitary CP (X -> X, Z -> Z^-1), an outer automorphism of the Narain space group that projects nothing. They induce multiplier-minus-one similitudes differing by -1 in Sp(2d,3), so they are the two implementations the TOE certificate found. Because CP projects nothing it cannot supply the even-order element the order-three no-goes require.

dictionary.X: lattice translation permuting the three fixed points of a T^2/Z3 plane
dictionary.Z: lattice translation acting by the space-group selection-rule phases
dictionary.centre: the order-three point-group element; equals the selection rule
dictionary.d planes: one shared centre, so 3^(1+2d) on 3^d fixed points; d = 2 gives the W(3,3) form

CP.action: X -> X, Z -> Z^-1, omega -> omega^-1

inversions.relation: they differ by -1 in Sp(2d,3), hence lie in the same multiplier-minus-one coset
